main.title: The Game Awards
main.subtitle: A shared archive of the work we remember
main.summary: A celebration of game makers, with every category winner from 2014 onward.

cards.heading: What the awards celebrate
cards.text: The Game Awards celebrates the people who make games: designers, artists, writers, performers, composers and the teams around them. Created by Geoff Keighley in 2014, the annual show combines awards with performances, announcements and conversations about the medium.

cards.heading: A changing medium, a shared stage
cards.text: An awards archive is also a record of changing priorities. Categories make room for new ways to play and new kinds of work, from independent production and performance to accessibility and community support. Move through the years to read every category winner, then open the official ceremony beside the list.

main.title: Yakuza: Like a Dragon
main.subtitle: Ichiban changes the rules of the series
main.summary: Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a 2020 role-playing video game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for the PlayStation 4.

cards.heading: A new hero and turn-based combat
cards.text: Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a 2020 role-playing video game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega for the PlayStation 4. The eighth mainline installment in the Yakuza series and the first to be developed as a turn-based RPG, it was released in Japan and Asia on January 16, 2020. The western release of the game for the PlayStation 4, Windows, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on November 10, 2020 included new costumes, the returning of English audio track for the first time since the first game, and some previously paid DLC. This version was then released in Japan and Asia under the subtitle International on February 25, 2021 for Windows and Xbox platforms. The game was released worldwide for the PlayStation 5 on March 2, 2021, and a version for Amazon Luna launched on December 10, 2021.

cards.heading: Ichiban Kasuga seeks a new beginning
cards.text: In contrast to previous Yakuza games that focused on the life of Kazuma Kiryu, a man trying to lead a normal life after leaving the yakuza lifestyle, Like a Dragon instead introduces a new protagonist named Ichiban Kasuga. After being imprisoned for 18 years only to then be betrayed by his former boss, Kasuga goes on a personal quest to become a "hero" and uncover the reason for his betrayal alongside his companions. Yakuza: Like a Dragon received positive reviews from both players and critics who praised the narrative, characters, gameplay, unique take on the JRPG sub-genre, and presentation.

cards.heading: The Japanese name goes international
cards.text: Yakuza: Like a Dragon is the first to use the Japanese title worldwide, albeit as a subtitle. The game was followed up by a 2023 spin-off, Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name, and a mainline sequel, Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, in 2024.

main.title: Dreams
main.subtitle: A place to make and play
main.summary: Dreams is Media Molecule's PlayStation 4 creation game, released on 14 February 2020. Players can build games, scenes, music and animated experiences, then share them with others. Browsing a creation and opening its parts belongs to the same environment, making play an introduction to what might be made next. An imp acts as the player's cursor and presence within the tools. The range extends from a small object to a complete playable world, with characters, sound and behaviour assembled inside the same console application.

cards.heading: A place to make and play
cards.text: Dreams is Media Molecule's PlayStation 4 creation game, released on 14 February 2020. Players can build games, scenes, music and animated experiences, then share them with others. Browsing a creation and opening its parts belongs to the same environment, making play an introduction to what might be made next. An imp acts as the player's cursor and presence within the tools. The range extends from a small object to a complete playable world, with characters, sound and behaviour assembled inside the same console application.

cards.heading: Build with another person’s starting point
cards.text: Objects and creations can be shared for reuse when their makers permit it. A player can take an existing element, change it and combine it with other work, making a larger project possible without constructing every part from nothing. Sculpting and painting give forms their appearance, while logic connects actions and responses. Music tools add another route into the process. The controller can be used through motion or analogue input, and the imp can enter a character so the maker can test the scene from inside it.

cards.heading: The collection keeps changing hands
cards.text: Media Molecule supplied tutorials and its own Art's Dream adventure to demonstrate how the tools could work together. Community curation helped guide players through the growing library, where small experiments could appear beside more complete games. That variety made Dreams as much a place to encounter other makers as a set of editing tools. The studio ended live development support in September 2023 while retaining the existing online service. Its history shows the possibilities and practical limits of making a creation platform whose work remains inside one console ecosystem.

main.title: Call of Duty: Warzone
main.subtitle: Verdansk Turns Call of Duty into a Shared Space
main.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone launched in March 2020 as a free-to-play game from Infinity Ward and Raven Software.

cards.heading: A free route into Verdansk
cards.text: Call of Duty: Warzone launched in March 2020 as a free-to-play game from Infinity Ward and Raven Software. At launch, up to 150 players entered Verdansk in teams of three. It supported crossplay, allowing the same match to bring together friends using PlayStation 4, Xbox One and PC.

cards.heading: Defeat can open another door
cards.text: The Gulag gave an eliminated player a one-on-one fight for a chance to return. Teammates could also spend in-match cash at Buy Stations to recover a fallen squad member. These systems made a defeat something the squad could respond to, instead of always ending that person's participation immediately.

cards.heading: Money changes the objective
cards.text: Cash paid for equipment and other advantages, while optional Contracts offered rewards for taking on another task. Plunder made collecting cash the central goal and allowed repeated respawns. The two launch modes used the same broad environment to produce different reasons to move, take a risk or help a teammate.

cards.heading: Plunder: collecting Cash against the clock
cards.text: In the Plunder mode, teams have to search for stacks of Cash scattered around the map to accumulate $1 million. Once found or if time is almost up, the game goes into overtime, multiplying all Cash sums by 1.5. The team who has gathered the most money when the clock runs out is declared the winner. Players respawn automatically in this gamemode. Players spawn with custom loadouts, similar to regular multiplayer modes.
